Base directory for this skill: /tmp/claude-1000/bundled-skills/2.1.289/7d0d1115aa2f3c052ace15bfde138b56/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

lastPrompt: Using the code in this repository, and the data in https://github.com/AEADataEditor/aea-supplement-migration, but working in ../packages-over-time, create data and figures that plot the number of pack…

content.text: Clear categories of non-research items. Let me check the remaining author-bearing administrative titles before settling the filter.

input.command:
cd /home/vilhuber/Workspace/Github/AEADataEditor/packages-over-time && cat > data/interwrk/explore2.R <<'EOF'
suppressMessages({library(dplyr);library(stringr);library(purrr)})
options(width=220)
d <- as_tibble(readRDS("data/interwrk/crossref_raw.Rds")) %>% distinct(doi,.keep_all=TRUE) %>%
  mutate(noauth = map_lgl(author, ~ is.null(.x) || length(.x)==0 || (is.data.frame(.x) && nrow(.x)==0)))
d %>% filter(!noauth, str_detect(title, regex("report|minutes|errat|correct|corrigend|retract|memoriam|obituar|fellow|award|introduction|note|editor|foreword|prize|lecture|address|reading|questionnaire|announce|policy|in honor|tribute|remembering", ignore_case=TRUE))) %>%
  mutate(t=str_trunc(title,90)) %>% count(t, sort=TRUE) %>% print(n=150)
EOF
docker run --rm --user $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -v $PWD:/w -w /w --entrypoint Rscript larsvilhuber/packages-over-time:2026-10-07 data/interwrk/explore2.R 2>&1

# Getting all openICPSR deposits that link to an AEA article
# openICPSR registers DOIs at DataCite with a relatedIdentifier pointing to the article DOI
#

source(file.path(rprojroot::find_rstudio_root_file(),"pathconfig.R"),echo=FALSE)
source(file.path(basepath,"global-libraries.R"),echo=FALSE)
source(file.path(programs,"libraries.R"), echo=FALSE)
source(file.path(programs,"config.R"), echo=FALSE)

# filenames in config.R

if ( download_datacite == TRUE ) {
  warning("Deleting existing DataCite file to force re-download.")
  if ( file.exists(datacite.raw.Rds) ) {
    file.remove(datacite.raw.Rds)
  }
}

if (file.exists(datacite.raw.Rds) ) {
  warning(paste("Re-using file:",datacite.raw.Rds))
} else {
  # cursor-based pagination through all matching records
  url <- modify_url(datacite.api,
                    query=list(`client-id`=datacite.client,
                               query=paste0("relatedIdentifiers.relatedIdentifier:",doi_prefix,"*"),
                               `page[size]`=1000,
                               `page[cursor]`=1,
                               `fields[dois]`="doi,publicationYear,registered,relatedIdentifiers"))
  pages <- list()
  while ( !is.null(url) ) {
    message(paste0("Fetching page ",length(pages)+1))
    resp <- RETRY("GET",url,times=5)
    stop_for_status(resp)
    js <- fromJSON(content(resp,as="text",encoding="UTF-8"),simplifyVector=FALSE)
    if ( length(js$data) == 0 ) break
    pages[[length(pages)+1]] <- js$data
    url <- js$links[["next"]]
  }
  records <- unlist(pages,recursive=FALSE)
  message(paste0("Retrieved ",length(records)," records"))
  saveRDS(records,file=datacite.raw.Rds)
}

records <- readRDS(datacite.raw.Rds)

# one row per (deposit DOI, related AEA DOI)
datacite.links <- map_dfr(records, function(r) {
  rel <- r$attributes$relatedIdentifiers
  if ( length(rel) == 0 ) return(NULL)
  tibble(datacite_doi      = tolower(r$attributes$doi),
         publicationYear   = as.integer(r$attributes$publicationYear %||% NA),
         registered        = r$attributes$registered %||% NA_character_,
         relationType      = map_chr(rel, ~ .x$relationType %||% NA_character_),
         relatedIdentifier = map_chr(rel, ~ .x$relatedIdentifier %||% NA_character_))
}) %>%
  mutate(relatedIdentifier = tolower(str_remove(relatedIdentifier,"^https?://(dx\\.)?doi\\.org/"))) %>%
  filter(str_starts(relatedIdentifier,paste0(doi_prefix,"/")))

# what relations are there?
datacite.links %>% count(relationType,sort=TRUE)

# Deposits are registered at several levels: the project (10.3886/E123456),
# its versions (10.3886/E123456V1, V2, ...), and sometimes individual files
# (10.3886/E123456V1-98765). A package is the project, regardless of version.
datacite.links <- datacite.links %>%
  mutate(level = case_when(str_detect(datacite_doi,"^10\\.3886/e\\d+$")        ~ "project",
                           str_detect(datacite_doi,"^10\\.3886/e\\d+v\\d+$")   ~ "version",
                           TRUE                                                ~ "other"),
         icpsr_project = str_extract(datacite_doi,"^10\\.3886/e\\d+"))

datacite.links %>% count(level)

write_csv(datacite.links,file=datacite.csv)

    distinct(doi,.keep_all=TRUE) %>%

    filter(!is.na(icpsr_doi)) %>%
    mutate(doi = tolower(doi))
  nrow(icpsr.refs)
  saveRDS(icpsr.refs, file= icpsr.refs.Rds)

  new.df <- new.df %>% select(-reference)
  saveRDS(new.df, file= crossref.raw.Rds)
  rm(new)
}
''')

# Getting openICPSR deposits that are AEA replication packages, from DataCite
# Two complementary queries:
#  1. deposits with a relatedIdentifier pointing to an AEA article DOI
#     (set for the migrated supplements and for deposits up to about 2020)
#  2. deposits whose title follows the AEA template ("Data and Code for: <article title>",
#     "Replication data for: ...", ...). Recent deposits often lack the link in (1);
#     they are matched to articles by title in 04_combine.R
#

source(file.path(rprojroot::find_rstudio_root_file(),"pathconfig.R"),echo=FALSE)
source(file.path(basepath,"global-libraries.R"),echo=FALSE)
source(file.path(programs,"libraries.R"), echo=FALSE)
source(file.path(programs,"config.R"), echo=FALSE)

# filenames in config.R

# cursor-based pagination through all matching records
fetch_datacite <- function(query) {
  url <- modify_url(datacite.api,
                    query=list(`client-id`=datacite.client,
                               query=query,
                               `page[size]`=1000,
                               `page[cursor]`=1,
                               `fields[dois]`="doi,titles,publicationYear,registered,relatedIdentifiers"))
  pages <- list()
  while ( !is.null(url) ) {
    message(paste0("Fetching page ",length(pages)+1))
    resp <- RETRY("GET",url,times=5)
    stop_for_status(resp)
    js <- fromJSON(content(resp,as="text",encoding="UTF-8"),simplifyVector=FALSE)
    if ( length(js$data) == 0 ) break
    pages[[length(pages)+1]] <- js$data
    url <- js$links[["next"]]
  }
  records <- unlist(pages,recursive=FALSE)
  message(paste0("Retrieved ",length(records)," records"))
  records
}

if ( download_datacite == TRUE ) {
  warning("Deleting existing DataCite files to force re-download.")
  for ( f in c(datacite.raw.Rds,datacite.titles.raw.Rds) ) {
    if ( file.exists(f) ) file.remove(f)
  }
}

if (file.exists(datacite.raw.Rds) ) {
  warning(paste("Re-using file:",datacite.raw.Rds))
} else {
  records <- fetch_datacite(paste0("relatedIdentifiers.relatedIdentifier:",doi_prefix,"*"))
  saveRDS(records,file=datacite.raw.Rds)
}

if (file.exists(datacite.titles.raw.Rds) ) {
  warning(paste("Re-using file:",datacite.titles.raw.Rds))
} else {
  records <- fetch_datacite(paste(paste0('titles.title:"',datacite.title.templates,'"'),collapse=" OR "))
  saveRDS(records,file=datacite.titles.raw.Rds)
}

# Deposits are registered at several levels: the project (10.3886/E123456),
# its versions (10.3886/E123456V1, V2, ...), and sometimes individual files
# (10.3886/E123456V1-98765). A package is the project, regardless of version.
add_level <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(level = case_when(str_detect(datacite_doi,"^10\\.3886/e\\d+$")        ~ "project",
                             str_detect(datacite_doi,"^10\\.3886/e\\d+v\\d+$")   ~ "version",
                             TRUE                                                ~ "other"),
           icpsr_project = str_extract(datacite_doi,"^10\\.3886/e\\d+"))
}

# --- (1) one row per (deposit DOI, related AEA DOI)

records <- readRDS(datacite.raw.Rds)

datacite.links <- map_dfr(records, function(r) {
  rel <- r$attributes$relatedIdentifiers
  if ( length(rel) == 0 ) return(NULL)
  tibble(datacite_doi      = tolower(r$attributes$doi),
         publicationYear   = as.integer(r$attributes$publicationYear %||% NA),
         registered        = r$attributes$registered %||% NA_character_,
         relationType      = map_chr(rel, ~ .x$relationType %||% NA_character_),
         relatedIdentifier = map_chr(rel, ~ .x$relatedIdentifier %||% NA_character_))
}) %>%
  mutate(relatedIdentifier = tolower(str_remove(relatedIdentifier,"^https?://(dx\\.)?doi\\.org/"))) %>%
  filter(str_starts(relatedIdentifier,paste0(doi_prefix,"/"))) %>%
  add_level()

# what relations are there? IsCitedBy are ICPSR studies (10.3886/ICPSR...)
# used as data by AEA articles, not replication packages
datacite.links %>% count(relationType,sort=TRUE)
datacite.links %>% count(level)

write_csv(datacite.links,file=datacite.csv)

# --- (2) one row per deposit DOI with an AEA-template title

records <- readRDS(datacite.titles.raw.Rds)

datacite.titles <- map_dfr(records, function(r) {
  tibble(datacite_doi    = tolower(r$attributes$doi),
         publicationYear = as.integer(r$attributes$publicationYear %||% NA),
         title           = r$attributes$titles[[1]]$title %||% NA_character_)
}) %>%
  add_level() %>%
  filter(level != "other") %>%
  # the article title is whatever follows the template prefix
  mutate(article_title = str_remove(title,regex(paste0("^.*?(",paste(datacite.title.templates,collapse="|"),")\\s*:?\\s*"),
                                                ignore_case=TRUE)))

datacite.titles %>% count(level)

write_csv(datacite.titles,file=datacite.titles.csv)

  }
}

if (file.exists(datacite.raw.Rds) ) {
  warning(paste("Re-using file:",datacite.raw.Rds))
} else {
  # cursor-based pagination through all matching records
  url <- modify_url(datacite.api,
                    query=list(`client-id`=datacite.client,

                               `page[size]`=1000,
                               `page[cursor]`=1,
                               `fields[dois]`="doi,publicationYear,registered,relatedIdentifiers"))
  pages <- list()
  while ( !is.null(url) ) {
    message(paste0("Fetching page ",length(pages)+1))
    resp <- RETRY("GET",url,times=5)
    stop_for_status(resp)
    js <- fromJSON(content(resp,as="text",encoding="UTF-8"),simplifyVector=FALSE)
    if ( length(js$data) == 0 ) break
    pages[[length(pages)+1]] <- js$data
    url <- js$links[["next"]]
  }
  records <- unlist(pages,recursive=FALSE)
  message(paste0("Retrieved ",length(records)," records"))
  saveRDS(records,file=datacite.raw.Rds)
}

# ===========================
# Packages
# ===========================

# Historical supplements migrated to openICPSR
migration <- readRDS(file.path(migrationloc,"migration_packages.Rds")) %>%
  transmute(doi,
            package = coalesce(str_extract(icpsr_doi,"^10\\.3886/e\\d+"),paste0("migration:",doi)),
            source  = "migration")

# Deposits at openICPSR linked to AEA articles (includes most of the migrated ones)
datacite <- read_csv(datacite.csv) %>%
  filter(relationType %in% c("IsSupplementTo","IsDocumentedBy")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(icpsr_project)) %>%
  transmute(doi=relatedIdentifier, package=icpsr_project, source="datacite") %>%
  distinct()

all.packages <- bind_rows(migration,datacite) %>%
  group_by(doi,package) %>%
  summarize(source = paste(sort(unique(source)),collapse="+"), .groups="drop")

all.packages %>% count(source)

# Attach article information. A package linked to several articles (rare)
# is counted once, with its earliest article.
packages <- all.packages %>%
  inner_join(articles %>% select(doi,year,Journal),by="doi") %>%
  arrange(package,year,doi) %>%
  distinct(package,.keep_all=TRUE)

# How many package-article links do not match a research article in scope?
all.packages %>% anti_join(articles,by="doi") %>% nrow()
nrow(packages)

saveRDS(packages,file=packages.Rds)
write_csv(packages,file=packages.csv)

# ===========================
# Tabulate by year and by journal x year
# ===========================

articles.flagged <- articles %>%
  left_join(packages %>% count(doi,name="n_packages"),by="doi") %>%
  mutate(n_packages = coalesce(n_packages,0L))

tabulate <- function(df, ...) {
  df %>%
    group_by(...) %>%
    summarize(articles              = n(),
              articles_with_package = sum(n_packages>0),
              packages              = sum(n_packages),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(pct_with_package = round(100*articles_with_package/articles,1))
}

by.year    <- tabulate(articles.flagged, year)
by.journal <- tabulate(articles.flagged, Journal, year)

by.year %>% print(n=Inf)

write_csv(by.year,   file=by_year.csv)
write_csv(by.journal,file=by_journal.csv)

# Figures: replication packages over time, overall and by journal
# Total research articles are shown as a faint benchmark
#

source(file.path(rprojroot::find_rstudio_root_file(),"pathconfig.R"),echo=FALSE)
source(file.path(basepath,"global-libraries.R"),echo=FALSE)
source(file.path(programs,"libraries.R"), echo=FALSE)
source(file.path(programs,"config.R"), echo=FALSE)

# filenames in config.R

by.year    <- read_csv(by_year.csv)    %>% filter(between(year,firstyear,lastyear))
by.journal <- read_csv(by_journal.csv) %>% filter(between(year,firstyear,lastyear))

journal.order <- c("AER","AER:Insights","AEA P&P",
                   "AEJ:Applied Economics","AEJ:Economic Policy","AEJ:Macro","AEJ:Micro",
                   "JEL","JEP")
by.journal <- by.journal %>% mutate(Journal=factor(Journal,levels=journal.order))

col.packages  <- "#2F6BAD"
col.benchmark <- "grey75"

caption.text <- paste0("Research articles: Crossref, excluding front matter, book reviews, and editorial/administrative notes.\n",
                       "Replication packages: AEA Data and Code Repository at openICPSR (DataCite, article references, migrated supplements).\n",
                       "By year of print publication, ",firstyear,"-",lastyear,".")

theme_packages <- function() {
  theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.line = element_line(linewidth=0),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour="grey92",linewidth=0.3),
          legend.position = "top",
          legend.justification = "left",
          legend.title = element_blank(),
          plot.caption = element_text(hjust=0,colour="grey40",size=7),
          plot.title.position = "plot",
          plot.caption.position = "plot")
}

# long format, so that the legend identifies both series
to_long <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    select(any_of("Journal"),year,articles,articles_with_package) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(articles,articles_with_package),names_to="series",values_to="n") %>%
    mutate(series=factor(series,levels=c("articles","articles_with_package"),
                         labels=c("All research articles","Articles with a replication package")))
}

fill.scale <- scale_fill_manual(values=c("All research articles"=col.benchmark,
                                         "Articles with a replication package"=col.packages))
alpha.scale <- scale_alpha_manual(values=c("All research articles"=0.45,
                                           "Articles with a replication package"=1),
                                  guide="none")

# ===========================
# Overall
# ===========================

by.year %>%
  to_long() %>%
  ggplot(aes(year,n,fill=series,alpha=series)) +
    # benchmark drawn first and wider, packages in front
    geom_col(data=~ filter(.x,series=="All research articles"),width=0.85) +
    geom_col(data=~ filter(.x,series!="All research articles"),width=0.55) +
    fill.scale + alpha.scale +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(firstyear,lastyear,5),expand=expansion(add=0.6)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels=label_comma(),expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0.05))) +
    labs(title="Replication packages in AEA journals, by year",
         x=element_blank(),y=element_blank(),caption=caption.text) +
    theme_packages() -> fig.packages.year

ggsave(file.path(Figures,"figure_packages_by_year.png"),fig.packages.year,width=8,height=5,dpi=300)
ggsave(file.path(Figures,"figure_packages_by_year.pdf"),fig.packages.year,width=8,height=5)

# ===========================
# By journal
# ===========================

by.journal %>%
  to_long() %>%
  ggplot(aes(year,n,fill=series,alpha=series)) +
    geom_col(data=~ filter(.x,series=="All research articles"),width=0.85) +
    geom_col(data=~ filter(.x,series!="All research articles"),width=0.55) +
    facet_wrap(~ Journal,ncol=3,scales="free_y") +
    fill.scale + alpha.scale +
    scale_x_continuous(limits=c(firstyear-0.5,lastyear+0.5),breaks=seq(firstyear,lastyear,10),
                       expand=expansion(add=0.2)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels=label_comma(),expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0.05))) +
    labs(title="Replication packages in AEA journals, by journal and year",
         subtitle="Vertical scales differ across panels. AEA P&P is published separately since 2018; earlier, it was the May issue of the AER.",
         x=element_blank(),y=element_blank(),caption=caption.text) +
    theme_packages() +
    theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(face="bold",hjust=0),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(colour="grey30",size=8.5),
          panel.spacing.x = unit(1,"lines")) -> fig.packages.journal

ggsave(file.path(Figures,"figure_packages_by_journal.png"),fig.packages.journal,width=10,height=8,dpi=300)
ggsave(file.path(Figures,"figure_packages_by_journal.pdf"),fig.packages.journal,width=10,height=8)

    theme(axis.line = element_line(linewidth=0),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour="grey92",linewidth=0.3),
          legend.position = "top",
          legend.justification = "left",
          legend.title = element_blank(),
          plot.caption = element_text(hjust=0,colour="grey40",size=7),
          plot.title.position = "plot",
          plot.caption.position = "plot")
}

# long format, so that the legend identifies both series
to_long <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    select(any_of("Journal"),year,articles,articles_with_package) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(articles,articles_with_package),names_to="series",values_to="n") %>%
    mutate(series=factor(series,levels=c("articles","articles_with_package"),
                         labels=c("All research articles","Articles with a replication package")))
}

fill.scale <- scale_fill_manual(values=c("All research articles"=col.benchmark,
                                         "Articles with a replication package"=col.packages))

                                           "Articles with a replication package"=1),
                                  guide="none")

# ===========================
# Overall
# ===========================

by.year %>%
  to_long() %>%
  ggplot(aes(year,n,fill=series,alpha=series)) +
    # benchmark drawn first and wider, packages in front

    geom_col(data=~ filter(.x,series!="All research articles"),width=0.55) +
    fill.scale + alpha.scale +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(firstyear,lastyear,5),expand=expansion(add=0.6)) +

# Replication packages in AEA journals over time

Counts, by year of print publication, the research articles published in AEA journals and the number of those articles that have a replication package in the [AEA Data and Code Repository](https://www.openicpsr.org/openicpsr/aea) at openICPSR. Figures show the article counts with a replication package, with the total number of research articles as a faint benchmark, overall and by journal.

Code patterns are derived from [aea-cumulative-summary](https://github.com/AEADataEditor/aea-cumulative-summary); historical supplement data from [aea-supplement-migration](https://github.com/AEADataEditor/aea-supplement-migration).

## Outputs

| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| `outputs/figures/figure_packages_by_year.{png,pdf}` | Articles with a replication package, by year, against all research articles |
| `outputs/figures/figure_packages_by_journal.{png,pdf}` | Same, by journal (vertical scales differ across panels) |
| `outputs/packages_by_year.csv` | `year`, `articles`, `articles_with_package`, `packages`, `pct_with_package` |
| `outputs/packages_by_journal_year.csv` | Same, by `Journal` and `year` |
| `outputs/packages_by_article.csv` | One row per package: article `doi`, openICPSR `package`, `source`, `year`, `Journal` |
| `data/crossref/crossref_dois.csv` | The research articles (the denominator) |

`articles_with_package` is what the figures plot. `packages` counts distinct openICPSR projects and can be slightly higher, because a few articles have several (for example, a comment and its reply, or a supplement re-deposited later). Figures cover `firstyear` through `lastyear` (the last complete year), set in `programs/config.R`; the CSV files include the current, partial year.

## Steps

All programs are in `programs/` and are run in order by `programs/main.sh`.

1. `01_get_crossref.R`: downloads all works since 2000 from Crossref for each journal, using both print and online ISSNs (individual works carry only one of them). Also extracts, from each article's reference list, citations of openICPSR deposits (`10.3886/E...`).
2. `02_get_migration.R`: downloads the mapping of historical supplements (formerly ZIP files on the AEA website) to openICPSR, from `aea-supplement-migration` (October 2019 batch and September 2021 final batch).
3. `03_get_datacite.R`: queries DataCite for openICPSR deposits (a) with a related identifier pointing to an AEA DOI and (b) with a title following the AEA template ("Data and Code for: ...", "Replication data for: ...").
4. `04_combine.R`: filters Crossref to research articles and matches packages to articles (see below); tabulates by year and by journal and year.
5. `05_figures.R`: creates the figures.

### Research articles (denominator)

From the Crossref records, the following are removed:

- records that are not of type `journal-article` (issue records)
- front matter (DOIs ending in `i`)
- records without authors (front matter, book review sections, committee reports, journal mastheads, ...)
- JEL book reviews (DOIs ending in `.r1`, `.r2`, ...)
- editorial and administrative content with authors, identified by title: forewords, editors' introductions and notes, reports of the editors, committees, treasurer, secretary, and Data Editor, minutes, auditor reports, corrigenda and errata, "Recommendations for Further Reading", and similar (the full list of patterns is in `04_combine.R`)

Comments and replies are kept. Before 2018, the Papers and Proceedings were the May issue of the AER, and are counted as AER; since 2018, they are counted as AEA P&P.

### Replication packages (numerator)

A package is an openICPSR project (all versions and file-level DOIs of `10.3886/E123456` count as one). A package is matched to an article by any of:

- `migration`: the migration of historical supplements (from `aea-supplement-migration`)
- `datacite`: the DataCite record of the deposit lists the article DOI as `IsSupplementTo` or `IsDocumentedBy`. ICPSR studies that AEA articles merely cite (`IsCitedBy`) are not counted. This link is missing for most deposits after about 2020.
- `reference`: the article's Crossref reference list cites the deposit, and the citation text contains the article's own title (the AEA requires that articles cite their replication package; articles may also cite other deposits as data sources)
- `title`: the deposit's title is "Data and Code for: *article title*" (or a similar template), the normalized title matches exactly one AEA research article, and the deposit was published no more than 3 years before or 2 years after the article

The `source` column in `outputs/packages_by_article.csv` records which methods matched each package.

## Running in Docker

The `Dockerfile` extends `rocker/tidyverse` and runs the project's own package initialization (`global-libraries.R`, `programs/libraries.R`). The image and tag are set in `.myconfig.sh`.

```bash
bash build.sh 2026-10-07       # build larsvilhuber/packages-over-time:2026-10-07
DOCKEREXTRA="--user $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp" bash run_docker.sh 2026-10-07 -c \
  'cd /home/rstudio/packages-over-time/programs && bash main.sh'
```

Set `download_crossref`, `download_migration`, and `download_datacite` in `programs/config.R` to `FALSE` to reuse previously downloaded data. A full run takes about 10 minutes, mostly for the Crossref download.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

content.text:
The data and figures are done in `../packages-over-time`. I ran the whole pipeline from scratch in its own Docker image (`larsvilhuber/packages-over-time:2026-10-07`, built from that folder's Dockerfile) and it finished without errors. Nothing is committed yet.

**Figures** (PNG and PDF):
- [figure_packages_by_year.png](../packages-over-time/outputs/figures/figure_packages_by_year.png): articles with a replication package as solid bars, with all research articles as faint grey bars behind them, 2000–2025.
- [figure_packages_by_journal.png](../packages-over-time/outputs/figures/figure_packages_by_journal.png): the same for each of the 9 journals, small multiples with a separate vertical scale per panel.

**Data:** `outputs/packages_by_year.csv`, `outputs/packages_by_journal_year.csv`, `outputs/packages_by_article.csv` (records how each package was matched to its article), and the filtered article list in `data/crossref/crossref_dois.csv`.

**Main results:** about 70–75% of research articles have a package from 2014 on. In 2025, 400 of 535 articles had one. Before 2004 almost none did.

**How the counts are built:**
- **Article benchmark:** the Crossref records with front matter, items without authors, JEL book reviews, and a list of editorial/administrative titles removed (forewords, editors' notes, reports, minutes, corrigenda, and similar). Comments and replies are kept. P&P articles before 2018 count as AER, since P&P was then the AER May issue.
- **Packages:** the migration data alone only covers supplements up to 2019. The DataCite links between packages and articles mostly stop after 2020, which made post-2021 coverage look like ~25%. I added two more ways to match:
  - the article's own Crossref references, which cite its package, and
  - openICPSR package titles of the form "Data and Code for: *article title*".
- **Packages vs. articles:** the figures plot *articles with at least one package*. A few articles have more than one package (for example a comment and its reply), so the CSV also has a `packages` column with the slightly higher count.
- **Additions to the copied code:** Crossref is queried with both print and online ISSNs for every journal, because JEL was missing most years under its online ISSN alone. AEA Papers and Proceedings is added as a separate journal.

**Bug in this repo:** `rcrossref::cr_journals()` stops after 5,000 records by default. AER has more than that since 2000, so 2023 was missing entirely and 2024 was partly missing. I fixed it in the new folder with `cursor_max = 100000`. `programs/11_get_crossref.R` in aea-cumulative-summary has the same truncation, and I didn't change it.

The README in the new folder describes each step, the filter, and how to run it in Docker.
fix it in the current folder as well. I'll rerun in a new session.

library(rcrossref)

issns[3,] <- c("American Economic Journal: Macroeconomics", "1945-7715",tmp.date)
issns[4,] <- c("American Economic Journal: Microeconomics", "1945-7685",tmp.date)
issns[5,] <- c("The American Economic Review","1944-7981",tmp.date)
issns[6,] <- c("The American Economic Review","0002-8282",tmp.date)  # print ISSN is needed!
issns[7,] <- c("Journal of Economic Literature","2328-8175",tmp.date)
issns[8,] <- c("Journal of Economic Perspectives","1944-7965",tmp.date)
issns[9,] <- c("American Economic Review: Insights","2640-2068",tmp.date)

  saveRDS(issns %>% filter(!is.na(journal)), file= issns.file)
} else {
  warning(paste("Reusing file: ",issns.file))
}

issns <- readRDS(file = issns.file)

if ( download_crossref == TRUE ) {
  warning("Deleting existing DOI file to force re-download.")
  if ( file.exists(doi.file.Rds) ) {
    file.remove(doi.file.Rds) 
  }
}


if (file.exists(doi.file.Rds) ) {
  warning(paste("Re-using file:",doi.file.Rds))
} else{
  new.df <- NA
  for ( x in 1:nrow(issns) ) {
    message(paste0("Processing ",issns[x,"journal"]," (",issns[x,"issn"],")"))
    new <- cr_journals(issn=issns[x,"issn"], works=TRUE,
                       filter=c(from_pub_date=issns[x,"lastdate"]),
                       select=c("DOI","title","published-print","volume","issue","container-title","author"),
                       .progress="text",
                       cursor = "*",
                       # default cursor_max is 5000, which truncates AER
                       cursor_max = 100000)
    if ( x == 1 ) {
      new.df <- as.data.frame(new$data)
      new.df$issn = issns[x,"issn"]
    } else {
      tmp.df <- as.data.frame(new$data)
      if ( nrow(tmp.df) > 0 ) {
        tmp.df$issn = issns[x,"issn"]
        new.df <- bind_rows(new.df,tmp.df)
      } else {
        warning(paste0("Did not find records for ISSN=",issns[x,"issn"]))
      }
      rm(tmp.df)
    }
  }
  # filters
  saveRDS(new.df, file=  file.path(interwrk,"new.Rds"))

}

  filter(str_sub(doi, start= -1)!="i")-> filtered.df
